title: The 45-minute LLD interview
idea: A low-level design (LLD) interview tests whether you can turn a vague problem into clear classes, a working core and sound trade-offs, while talking through each step.
points: Spend the first minutes asking questions and writing a short requirement list.
Name the entities and one interface where behaviour will vary.
Code the core use case end to end, then demo it and name extensions.
Practise classic prompts the same way: parking lot, elevator, vending machine, library, rate limiter.

items.label: Clarify, ~5 min
items.text: Ask about actors, scale and edge cases. Write the agreed requirements down.

items.label: Model, ~10 min
items.text: Nouns become classes, verbs become methods. Sketch one key interface.

items.label: Code, ~20 min
items.text: Write the service, entities and one strategy, with `private final` fields.

items.label: Demo, ~5 min
items.text: Trace one call through `main` and say what prints, including a failure.

items.label: Extend, ~5 min
items.text: Answer follow-ups: show which class changes and which stays untouched.

code.title: Practice: parcel locker
code.caption: A practice problem sized for an interview: assign each parcel the smallest free locker that fits.

walk.text: Model first: an `enum` for sizes and a `record` for an immutable locker.
The one place behaviour may vary becomes an interface: how to pick a locker.
`SmallestFit` keeps only lockers big enough, then takes the smallest by enum order.
The service owns state and receives its policy through the constructor.
`deposit` filters free lockers, asks the policy, records the parcel, reports the result.
The demo: three lockers, four requests, including one that cannot be served.

pitfalls: Do not start coding before the interviewer agrees on the requirement list.
Avoid drawing every pattern you know; add one only when a requirement asks for it.
Keep talking while you code, so the interviewer hears each trade-off you make.

quiz.q: In the locker demo, what does the second request print?
quiz.why: L1 is taken by p1. L2 and L3 both fit a small parcel; `min` by size picks MEDIUM L3 over LARGE L2.

takeaway: Clarify, model, code the core, demo it, then extend on request.

starters: What questions should I ask in the first five minutes?
